findings.claim: Variable names are not restricted to identifier characters. RoutePattern.parse takes everything after ':' up to the next '/' as the name, so the Express-style patterns '/:id.json' or '/:from-:to' register without error and produce one parameter named 'id.json' / 'from-:to'. A wave-3 handler calling req.param("id") then gets null without any warning. The SRS and object.md say nothing about the variable-name charset, so this is a spec gap that the implementation fills silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a decision (SRS clarification): either reject a variable name that is not [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* with RoutingConfigException at registration, or document in docs/api/routing.md that the whole segment after ':' is the name. Mark it (미확정) until decided.

findings.claim: Pattern literals are compared against once-decoded request segments, but parse() accepts literals that no valid request can ever match (a '%' escape such as '/a%20b' or '/a%2Fb', raw space, '#', control chars). Express matches '/a%20b' against the encoded path, so an Express user porting such a route gets a route that never matches and no configuration error.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject literals containing '%', '#' or chars <= 0x20 / 0x7F at registration (same RoutingConfigException path), or document that pattern literals are written decoded (as docs/api/routing.md already shows with '/café').

findings.claim: Router.allowFor is public, takes no lock and has no frozen check. Before freeze() it iterates the mutable ArrayList that synchronized add() is growing, so a concurrent call can throw ConcurrentModificationException or see a half-built table. It can also include TRACE/CONNECT routes that freeze() would reject. lookup guards against this with its frozen check; allowFor does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same 'if (!frozen) throw IllegalStateException' guard to allowFor, or make it package-private (the only callers are tests and lookup's own Allow path already uses allowOf).
